quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the flight was delayed by three hours, the family still made it to the wedding on time.
quests.sentence: ____ the flight was delayed by three hours, the family still made it to the wedding on time.
quests.hint: Making it on time despite the long delay is the surprising part - think about which connector introduces an unexpected contrast like that.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession - despite the delay, they still arrived on time. 'Because' would incorrectly frame the delay as the reason for arriving on time, which reverses the logic.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ it didn't fit the budget she had set for the trip, Maria loved the vintage jacket.
quests.sentence: ____ it didn't fit the budget she had set for the trip, Maria loved the vintage jacket.
quests.hint: This contrast clause comes first, before the main statement - which connector can open a sentence like that?
quests.explanation: 'Although' can introduce a concession clause at the very start of a sentence. 'But' and 'yet' link two independent clauses and conventionally can't open a sentence this way.
quests.grammarRule: Concession - although (can begin a sentence, unlike but/yet)

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: Jason accepted the job offer ____ the salary was lower than he had hoped.
quests.sentence: Jason accepted the job offer ____ the salary was lower than he had hoped.
quests.hint: Accepting despite the lower salary is the unexpected part - not a reason, result, or added fact.
quests.explanation: 'Although' shows he accepted despite the disappointing salary. 'So' would wrongly suggest the lower salary caused him to accept, which reverses the logic.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ she'd never skied before, Elena handled the beginner slope pretty well.
quests.sentence: ____ she'd never skied before, Elena handled the beginner slope pretty well.
quests.hint: Her lack of experience makes her decent performance a pleasant surprise - a concession, not a cause.
quests.explanation: 'Though' works just like 'although' here, introducing a concession. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest her lack of experience caused her good performance.
quests.grammarRule: Concession - though (same as although, more casual)

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: I don't really like horror movies ____ I'll probably still go see the new one with you.
quests.sentence: I don't really like horror movies ____ I'll probably still go see the new one with you.
quests.hint: This sounds like casual spoken conversation - which of these two near-identical connectors fits that relaxed tone slightly better?
quests.explanation: 'Though' feels natural in casual speech like this. 'Although' means the same thing but tends to sound a touch more formal or written.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The stock dropped sharply last quarter ____ analysts remain optimistic about its long-term growth.
quests.sentence: The stock dropped sharply last quarter ____ analysts remain optimistic about its long-term growth.
quests.hint: Analysts staying hopeful despite the drop is the surprising, contrary part here.
quests.explanation: 'Though' introduces this concession between the recent drop and the continued optimism. 'And' would just add the two facts without showing the contrast.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the medication made her drowsy, Grace insisted on driving herself home.
quests.sentence: ____ the medication made her drowsy, Grace insisted on driving herself home.
quests.hint: Insisting on driving despite the drowsiness is a strong, almost stubborn contrast - which connector best emphasizes that?
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasizes a stronger concession than plain 'although' - here, her insistence despite a real safety risk. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest the drowsiness was her reason for driving.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ he'd been rejected by twelve companies in a row, Marcus refused to give up on his job search.
quests.sentence: ____ he'd been rejected by twelve companies in a row, Marcus refused to give up on his job search.
quests.hint: The repeated string of rejections calls for extra emphasis - which connector intensifies the contrast more than a plain 'although' would?
quests.explanation: 'Even though' adds emphasis to the concession, fitting the weight of twelve rejections in a row. 'Although' would also work, but sounds comparatively flatter given how extreme this situation is.
quests.grammarRule: Concession - even though vs although (degree of emphasis)

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ both kids were exhausted from the trip, they refused to go to bed before finishing their video game level.
quests.sentence: ____ both kids were exhausted from the trip, they refused to go to bed before finishing their video game level.
quests.hint: Refusing to sleep despite total exhaustion is the surprising, almost stubborn twist here.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' introduces this strong concession between their exhaustion and their stubborn refusal to sleep. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest the exhaustion was their reason for staying up.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the initial results were promising, further testing revealed significant flaws in the design.
quests.sentence: ____ the initial results were promising, further testing revealed significant flaws in the design.
quests.hint: This reads like a formal report - which of the two near-identical connectors fits that more formal tone better?
quests.explanation: 'Although' suits this formal, written register. 'Though' means the same thing but tends to feel more conversational, less fitting for a technical report.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: I'm pretty tired ____ I could probably stay up a bit longer if you need help.
quests.sentence: I'm pretty tired ____ I could probably stay up a bit longer if you need help.
quests.hint: This is a relaxed, spoken-style message - the more casual of the two near-identical connectors usually fits better here.
quests.explanation: 'Though' fits this casual, conversational tone naturally. 'Because' would incorrectly frame the second clause as the reason for being tired.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the team was missing three starting players due to injury, they still won the championship game.
quests.sentence: ____ the team was missing three starting players due to injury, they still won the championship game.
quests.hint: Losing three starters is a serious setback - the win despite that deserves the stronger of these two near-identical connectors.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasizes the significant obstacle the team overcame. 'Although' would also technically work, but doesn't carry quite the same weight of emphasis given how serious the setback was. 'But' can't grammatically open the sentence this way.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ Tom prefers waking up early to exercise, his sister does all her workouts late at night.
quests.sentence: ____ Tom prefers waking up early to exercise, his sister does all her workouts late at night.
quests.hint: This sentence compares two different habits side by side, without suggesting either is unexpected or surprising.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally compares two contrasting facts or preferences. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest one habit causes the other, which isn't the relationship here.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the marketing team exceeded its targets this quarter, the sales team fell noticeably short.
quests.sentence: ____ the marketing team exceeded its targets this quarter, the sales team fell noticeably short.
quests.hint: This is comparing two separate, contrasting results side by side - not describing an unexpected outcome despite some obstacle.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' simply compares the two contrasting results. 'Although' would suggest one team succeeded despite some difficulty, which isn't what this sentence describes.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast vs Concession - whereas, not although

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: Some cultures eat their largest meal at midday, ____ others save it for the evening.
quests.sentence: Some cultures eat their largest meal at midday, ____ others save it for the evening.
quests.hint: Two different customs are simply being compared here, with neither causing the other.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' compares these two different meal customs. 'And' would just add the second fact without highlighting the contrast between them.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: My brother is incredibly organized, ____ I tend to leave everything until the last minute.
quests.sentence: My brother is incredibly organized, ____ I tend to leave everything until the last minute.
quests.hint: This sentence compares two personality traits in a casual, everyday way - not a formal report.
quests.explanation: 'While' can compare two contrasting facts in everyday speech, much like 'whereas' does more formally. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest one trait causes the other.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ urban populations have grown steadily over the past decade, rural populations in the same region have declined.
quests.sentence: ____ urban populations have grown steadily over the past decade, rural populations in the same region have declined.
quests.hint: This reads like a formal report comparing statistics - the more formal of the two comparison connectors fits best.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' suits this formal, academic tone well. 'While' would also technically work but feels less suited to this precise, report-like statement.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: One twin loves spicy food, ____ the other can't handle even a little bit of pepper.
quests.sentence: One twin loves spicy food, ____ the other can't handle even a little bit of pepper.
quests.hint: Two very different taste preferences are simply being compared here, nothing more.
quests.explanation: 'While' compares these two contrasting preferences. 'So' would incorrectly suggest one preference caused the other.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the weather forecast predicted storms all weekend, the hikers completed their trip without a single drop of rain.
quests.sentence: ____ the weather forecast predicted storms all weekend, the hikers completed their trip without a single drop of rain.
quests.hint: This describes an unexpected outcome that goes against what was predicted - not simply two different facts being compared.
quests.explanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the stormy forecast and the actual dry trip. 'Whereas' would only work for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not for this kind of unexpected twist.
quests.grammarRule: Concession vs Contrast - although, not whereas

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The cost of living in the capital has risen sharply, ____ wages in the same city have barely changed in five years.
quests.sentence: The cost of living in the capital has risen sharply, ____ wages in the same city have barely changed in five years.
quests.hint: Two separate trends are being compared here - rising costs and stagnant wages - not one thing happening despite another.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' compares these two parallel economic trends. 'Although' would suggest one trend happened despite some obstacle, which isn't quite the relationship being described.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast vs Concession - whereas, not although

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the new curriculum looked excellent on paper, teachers struggled to implement it with such limited classroom resources.
quests.sentence: ____ the new curriculum looked excellent on paper, teachers struggled to implement it with such limited classroom resources.
quests.hint: The struggle to implement it despite how good it looked on paper is the unexpected twist - not simply two facts being compared.
quests.explanation: 'Although' captures this concession between the promising design and the real struggle to use it. 'Whereas' would only fit if two separate, parallel facts were simply being compared side by side.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The laptop kept overheating ____ the cooling fan was clogged with dust.
quests.sentence: The laptop kept overheating ____ the cooling fan was clogged with dust.
quests.hint: This clause explains the reason for the overheating, not a contrast or comparison.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for the overheating. 'Although' or 'whereas' would incorrectly frame this as some kind of contrast rather than a straightforward cause.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The toddler cried at daycare drop-off every morning ____ he finally got used to the new routine after a few weeks.
quests.sentence: The toddler cried at daycare drop-off every morning ____ he finally got used to the new routine after a few weeks.
quests.hint: The crying continued right up to the point when he adjusted - not because of it, and not in contrast to it.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows the crying lasted up to the moment he got used to the routine. 'So' would incorrectly suggest the crying caused him to adjust.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the new park was beautifully designed, very few residents actually used it due to its distance from public transport.
quests.sentence: ____ the new park was beautifully designed, very few residents actually used it due to its distance from public transport.
quests.hint: The low usage despite the beautiful design is the unexpected twist - not two facts simply being compared.
quests.explanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the appealing design and the disappointing usage. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the proposal had several weak points, the board approved it anyway due to time pressure.
quests.sentence: ____ the proposal had several weak points, the board approved it anyway due to time pressure.
quests.hint: This concession clause opens the sentence - which connector can grammatically start a sentence like this?
quests.explanation: 'Although' can introduce a concession clause at the very start of a sentence. 'But,' 'yet,' and 'so' link two independent clauses and can't be used to open a sentence this way.
quests.grammarRule: Concession - although (structural: can front, unlike but/yet/so)

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The apartment is a bit small, ____ the location is absolutely perfect for what I need.
quests.sentence: The apartment is a bit small, ____ the location is absolutely perfect for what I need.
quests.hint: This is a casual, conversational remark - which everyday contrast word fits best here, rather than the more formal subordinating option?
quests.explanation: 'But' is the natural, neutral choice for this casual observation. 'Although' would also be grammatically fine, but sounds slightly more formal than this relaxed remark calls for.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ her test results were completely normal, the doctor still recommended a follow-up appointment just to be safe.
quests.sentence: ____ her test results were completely normal, the doctor still recommended a follow-up appointment just to be safe.
quests.hint: The extra caution despite normal results is the unexpected twist - not a reason, a simple comparison, or a result.
quests.explanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the normal results and the doctor's cautious follow-up. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest the normal results were the reason for the follow-up, which reverses the logic.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the renovation had gone smoothly for the first two months, a burst pipe in March set the entire project back by several weeks.
quests.sentence: ____ the renovation had gone smoothly for the first two months, a burst pipe in March set the entire project back by several weeks.
quests.hint: The unexpected setback after a smooth start is the surprising twist here, not a simple comparison or a reason.
quests.explanation: 'Although' captures the concession between the smooth start and the unexpected setback. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel situations, not this kind of sudden reversal.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: Solar panel adoption has surged in sunny southern regions, ____ colder northern areas have leaned more toward wind energy.
quests.sentence: Solar panel adoption has surged in sunny southern regions, ____ colder northern areas have leaned more toward wind energy.
quests.hint: Two different regional trends are simply being compared here, with neither happening despite the other.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting regional trends. 'Although' would suggest one trend happened despite some obstacle, which isn't the relationship being described here.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast vs Concession - whereas, not although

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: New volunteers can complete the online training module ____ attend one of the in-person orientation sessions.
quests.sentence: New volunteers can complete the online training module ____ attend one of the in-person orientation sessions.
quests.hint: These are two different ways to complete the same requirement - you'd only need to do one.
quests.explanation: 'Or' presents the online module and in-person session as alternative ways to meet the same requirement. 'And' would incorrectly suggest doing both is required.
